headline: On the study's most complex CSS the static-class lanes converge at 0.838-0.871 ms/1k, and what separates the rest is whether the library hashes at render (`emotion` 5.82) or writes its selector text into the class attribute (`bamboo` 2.21, `panda` 2.38).

microbench.why: Sixteen elements per group and every modern selector feature. `vanilla`, the css-prop fold and `stylex-layers` cluster at 0.838-0.871 ms/1k with nothing on the render path. The styled fold drops to 1.77 because `styled(Tabs)` gives folding a component host it cannot resolve, leaving a `Yak` wrapper worth 0.945 ms of library slice. `bamboo` and `panda` pay here for readable atomic names: the selector text lands inside the class attribute, so their markup carries 41 escaped ampersands and 32 escaped quotes in the two-group snapshot and react-dom's slice reaches 76.6 and 90.6 ms against `stylex-layers`' 32.9 with hashed names.

autocannon.why: `vanilla` serves 720 req/s and the css-prop fold 672, while the styled fold's residual `Yak` holds it to 433. `bamboo` (223), `panda` (190) and `tailwind-merge` (190) all write kilobyte class attributes per response, 8.02 kB of markup for `bamboo` against `vanilla`'s 1.14 kB. `emotion` at 135 req/s re-hashes the whole group.

top3.label: StyleX without CSS layers (:not() specificity hack)

attribution.why: `vanilla` renders in 1.33 ms and the css-prop fold in 1.48 with a 0.191 ms library slice. `emotion` is the worst shipped lane at 7.51 ms, where `@emotion/hash` alone is 82.0 ms of a 215 ms JS window and `@emotion/styled` another 31.9, and `styled-components` puts 103 ms into its own package. `bamboo` has essentially no library slice (0.011 ms) and still costs 3.24 ms, because 76.6 of its 88.8 ms of JS is react-dom writing and escaping the class attribute.

top3.label: StyleX without CSS layers (:not() specificity hack)

hydrate.why: Static sheets hydrate as pure JS at 48.1-51.1 ms. `goober` (199 ms) and `styled-components` (206 ms) inject during hydration and the span records 2.25-2.33 ms of style recalculation plus a 3.5-3.9 ms layout pass, the heaviest browser work in any hydration span in the study. `emotion` at 102 ms serializes on the client without forcing the same layout.

inp.why: Switching the active tab re-renders one group, and every build-time lane does it in 6.7-8.1 ms with under 1 ms of JS. `emotion` calls `@emotion/hash` and `@emotion/styled` for 0.563 ms each and lands at 28.1 ms, `goober` at 15.2 and `styled-components` at 12.0. Inside the fast cluster the ordering is noise.

top3.label: StyleX without CSS layers (:not() specificity hack)

mount.why: Cold mount parses the study's largest sheets. The extracted lanes mount at 95.1-99.6 ms, while `emotion` (232 ms), `styled-components` (209 ms) and `goober` (204 ms) build the sheet in the browser and their mount spans show 1.6-1.7 ms of style recalculation against the others' 0.9. `bamboo` mounts at 99.6 ms, inside the fast cluster, because its sheet is a file.

renderTiming.why: Chrome recalculates style once for every lane, but the runtime injectors lay out twice: `emotion`, `goober` and `styled-components` each record a second layout pass, the reflow their sheet injection forces. Their recalc also costs more, 1.62-1.70 ms against 0.87-0.96 ms for the static-sheet lanes.

payload.why: The css-prop fold ships 2.37 kB gzipped, the smallest in the study, one class per element however deep the rule chain. `vanilla` follows at 2.69 kB and the styled fold at 3.46. Atomic and utility naming is an order of magnitude worse on CSS this dense, `stylex-layers` 8.14 kB, `bamboo` 12.0 kB, `panda` 15.1 kB, `cnfast` 22.0 kB.

top3.label: StyleX without CSS layers (:not() specificity hack)

nsweep.why: At 4000 groups `vanilla` (30.7 ms) and both StyleX builds (30.9-32.1 ms) lead, with the css-prop fold at 33.5. The styled fold's residual `Yak` scales with n to 64.3 ms. `emotion` reaches 195 ms and `styled-components` 163, their per-render hash multiplied by 4000 groups.

crossCase: `tabs` is the single-file twin of the Example `multifile-composition` below. Nothing that matters crosses the module boundary: `vanilla`, `stylex-layers`, `bamboo` and the css-prop fold render and ship identical bytes in both (2.37 kB gzipped either way), and the styled fold's library slice is 0.945 against 0.925 ms. What costs the styled fold in this pair is the `styled(Tabs)` seam, which folding cannot resolve to an intrinsic tag, not the import.
